If you are the only parent, you can delete the whole household from the same place. Every member account, all household information, uploaded photos, paired tablets, invitations and calendar connections are deleted, and old links (calendar feed, sitter share link) stop working. Short-lived security counters, such as limits on repeated sign-in attempts, expire on their own.

If you turn on the morning summary (Settings, Notifications; it is off unless you turn it on), we also send you one short email a day, to a confirmed address only, with your own chores for the day, today's family events and tonight's dinner. Every summary email tells you how to turn it off.

If your household turns on the food inventory, we keep the items you add (name, amount, where it is kept, category, best-before or use-by date, and when it was bought or opened) and a short history of what was used up or thrown away, with who did it and when, so it can be undone. Everyone in the household can see it, and it is part of every member's data download. It is deleted with the household. Removing an item also removes its history.

In Settings, Privacy & data, choose Data Export. You get one file with all your information that you can open or keep (JSON format). Each member of the household downloads their own copy.

In Settings, Privacy & data, choose Delete Account and confirm with your password. Your account, sign-ins, messages, notifications and your own chores are deleted. Things you added for the household (events, lists, meals, notes, photos you uploaded) stay with the household under another parent.

is in a small beta, a parent can choose to share usage counts so we can check the app is working for families. They are off unless a parent turns them on under Settings, Privacy & data, "Share beta usage counts". When they are on, we keep one number per day for your household for each of these: events added, meals planned, chores assigned, chores completed, chores checked by a parent, rewards claimed, members who joined, and whether the household's first chore was assigned within 10 minutes of signing up. That is all: no names, no user accounts, no roles, no chore, event, meal or reward titles, no messages or photos, and nothing about which member did what.

reads and writes events with Google or Microsoft: it brings that calendar's events into the family calendar and, if the parent turns it on, adds family events to it. Each event shares its title, time, place and notes. We keep the access Google or Microsoft gives us encrypted and use it only for this sync. We do not read your other calendars, email or contacts. Disconnecting in Settings stops the sync, removes the events it brought in, and asks Google to cancel the access. Use of information received from Google follows the Google API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements.

Uploads are not public: the app only shows them to signed-in members of your household.

The counts are kept for 13 months. Older days are never used, and are deleted the next time your household's counts change. Turning the setting off deletes all of your household's counts straight away, and they are deleted with the household. They are part of every member's data download. They are never sold or shared with anyone, and they are separate from any other analytics.

We do not show ads, sell your information or use tracking pixels. We do not record which pages or screens you open. Older versions of the app kept a log of page visits; those records are deleted 90 days after they were made.

We only send emails you need: confirming your email address, resetting your password, household invites and the notifications you have left on. We never send marketing email. You can turn notification emails off in Settings.

Weather is off unless a parent turns it on in Family settings. When it is on, our server sends the place the parent chose, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo (open-meteo.com) to get the forecast. It also sends the place name a parent types when searching for a town. No names, accounts or other household information are sent. Turning weather off or removing the place stops these requests and deletes the saved forecast.

When someone changes household settings (turns a feature on or off, sends or cancels an invite, joins the household or deletes their account, changes the Today board, turns beta usage counts on or off, or pairs, renames or removes a family tablet), we keep a short line saying what changed, who did it and when. It holds names (of a feature, a member or a tablet) but never email addresses, codes, places or messages. Only parents can see it, under Settings, Recent changes. It is kept for 12 months and then deleted, and it is deleted with the household. It is part of a parent's data download; a teen's or child's download has only the lines about their own changes.
